source_refs.note: Exercise 4.2, Question 19: book p. 134 (Q2-Q25 general solutions and IVPs); answer key p. 303 (keys numbered 2-29)

blocks.prompt: 19 Find the general solution of the differential equation \(y - x\frac{dy}{dx} = 3\left(1 + x\frac{dy}{dx}\right)\).
blocks.explanation:
After collecting the \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) terms the equation becomes \(y - 3 = 4x\frac{dy}{dx}\): the \(y\)-part and the \(x\)-part can be separated.
(The constant 3 means it is not homogeneous; it is separable.)
Plan: collect \(\frac{dy}{dx}\), separate, integrate, remove the logarithms.
steps:
Given: \(y - x\frac{dy}{dx} = 3\left(1 + x\frac{dy}{dx}\right)\).
To find: the general solution.
Method: Separable equation (Section 4.2.1): write it as \(\frac{dy}{h(y)} = g(x)\,dx\) and integrate both sides.

Open the bracket and collect \(\frac{dy}{dx}\)
\[y - x\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 3 + 3x\dfrac{dy}{dx}\]
\[y - 3 = 4x\dfrac{dy}{dx}\]
Why: move \(-x\frac{dy}{dx}\) to the right and 3 to the left: \(3x\frac{dy}{dx} + x\frac{dy}{dx} = 4x\frac{dy}{dx}\).

Separate the variables
\[\dfrac{dy}{y - 3} = \dfrac{dx}{4x}\]
Why: divide by \(4x(y - 3)\) (assuming \(y \neq 3\)); \(y\)-terms with \(dy\), \(x\)-terms with \(dx\).

Remove the logarithms
\[y - 3 = Cx^{1/4}\]
\[y = 3 + Cx^{1/4}\]
Why: equal logarithms mean equal numbers; the sign \(\pm\) is absorbed into \(C\) (and \(C = 0\) gives the solution \(y = 3\)). Here \(x > 0\).

Check
\[y' = \tfrac{C}{4}x^{-3/4}\]
\[4xy' = Cx^{1/4} = y - 3\]
So \(y - 3 = 4xy'\), which is the given equation rearranged \(\checkmark\)
Why: substituting the answer back satisfies the equation.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key prints this answer as number 22, not 19. The Exercise 4.2 keys are numbered 2 to 29 for 25 questions (key 2 answers Question 1, and the extra keys 15, 19 and 27 match no printed question), so look for this answer under 22. The answer itself, \(y = 3 + Cx^{1/4}\), is correct.
